newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 21.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Monday.

- New information about Dunnes Stores payments to politicians will emerge from the tribunal of inquiry when it proceeds to take oral evidence from its first witness, Ben Dunne, today. - Services involving child care, elective admissions to hospitals and facilities for the mentally-handicapped will be seriously affected by a strike of 3,500 paramedics due to begin today.
- Police are warning traders and the public to be vigilant after the discovery of several thousand pounds worth of good-quality counterfeit bank notes.
- Allied Irish Banks is interested in buying the British Co-Operative Bank for a price estimated between 250 million and 300 million sterling.
- There has been a sharp drop in tourist enquiries and revenue from overseas for the first three months of this year, according to an internal Irish Tourist Board report.
- Ireland's main opposition party, Fianna Fail, will make a major push to prevent the Dunnes payments tribunal adjourning for the duration of the general election campaign.

- Allied Irish Banks denied it had reached agreement with the Galileo Group in the UK on the purchase of the Co-Op Bank for between 350 million and 400 million sterling but indicated its interest in the British bank.
- Government strategists are backing June 6 as election day in a bid to counter Fianna Fail charges that the Dunne Stores inquiry will be exploited for political advantage.
- The dispute at Irish Life took a dramatic turn last night as management confirmed it was considering dismissing 320 striking workers.
- Chaos in the health services is expected today as a national strike by more than 3,000 paramedics gets underway.
- Avonmore's hopes of avoiding a repeat of their failed 1991 merger proposal with Waterford Foods are beginning to look decidedly shaky.
